content.user_title: Map Code and Architecture with Mermaid
content.value_statement: Complex code and documentation can be difficult to understand quickly. This skill turns inspected relationships, flows, and structures into focused Mermaid diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Creates Mermaid diagrams from named code or documentation sources.
Selects flowchart, sequence, class, ER, state, or journey diagrams when appropriate.
Maps diagram nodes and edges to inspected source material.
Produces up to two diagrams for product, journey, or architecture documentation requests.
Explains what each generated diagram represents.
limitations: It cannot accurately diagram sources that were not provided or inspected.
It does not invent missing architecture or create a missing PRODUCT.md file.
It may split oversized relationships into simpler graphs.
It returns chat output unless the user provides a file path.

use_cases.title: Explain an unfamiliar codebase
use_cases.description: Ask for a relationship or flow diagram after naming the relevant files. Use the result to orient yourself before making changes.

use_cases.title: Document system architecture
use_cases.description: Provide architecture documents and named MDX sources to create concise diagrams that expose components, dependencies, and contradictions.

use_cases.title: Clarify a business journey
use_cases.description: Name the journey documentation and request a suitable Mermaid diagram that shows states, decisions, and transitions from the source material.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Diagram a file
prompt_templates.prompt: Read `src/checkout.ts` and create a Mermaid diagram showing the main control flow. Explain the diagram in three short sentences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you need a first visual overview of one source file.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Map dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the named API and service files. Create a Mermaid diagram showing how requests move between the controller, service, and data layer. Use only relationships supported by the files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when tracing a feature across several modules.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compare documentation and code
prompt_templates.prompt: Read `PRODUCT.md`, the named MDX files, and the relevant code. Produce up to two Mermaid diagrams, identify contradictions between documentation and code, and do not propose a new methodology.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when validating documented architecture against implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Model a complex workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the named sources and choose the Mermaid diagram type that best matches the question. Keep labels short, split oversized graphs, cite the inspected relationships in the explanation, and avoid inventing missing architecture.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a large system needs a focused, evidence-based visual model.

output_examples.input: Show how a login request moves through the web application.
output_examples.output: A Mermaid flow diagram showing the browser, login endpoint, authentication service, and session store, followed by a short explanation of each transition.

output_examples.input: Visualize the states in the order fulfillment workflow.
output_examples.output: A Mermaid state diagram showing pending, paid, packed, shipped, delivered, and cancelled states, with transitions tied to the inspected workflow documentation.

best_practices: Name the exact files or documentation sources that should be inspected.
Ask for a diagram type only when it matches the question.
Keep diagrams focused and require explanations grounded in the sources.
anti_patterns: Do not request architecture that the provided sources do not support.
Do not combine unrelated systems into one oversized diagram.
Do not treat a generated diagram as evidence for undocumented behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces Mermaid diagrams and a short explanation based on named code or documentation sources.

faq.question: Which diagram types are supported?
faq.answer: It can choose flowchart, sequence, class, ER, state, or journey diagrams when the source and question support them.

faq.question: Can it inspect an entire repository?
faq.answer: It focuses on named code or documentation sources. Provide relevant paths for a reliable result.

faq.question: Can it create PRODUCT.md?
faq.answer: No. It must not invent or create a missing PRODUCT.md file.

faq.question: How many diagrams can it create?
faq.answer: For product, journey, or architecture documentation requests, it creates at most two diagrams.

faq.question: Does it write files?
faq.answer: It returns chat output unless you provide a file path for the requested output.
